doc.title: Jake Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

title: Adjusting dynamics for each soloist
summary: Varying sticks, brushes and volume behind each player at the party, letting McKenna and Sutton take the lead.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Well I really enjoyed listening last night because I noticed that as each horn player got to do their thing, that you would vary what you were doing.
Yeah. I’d slow down or speed up, you know.

Oh yeah. Drown them out, it’s too loud here, too quiet here. Sure. Yeah. Well all the guys here have very good time, you know. Joe Temperley is fantastic. You know he’s really a hell of a player, that guy.
I know but you’d move from sticks to brushes, to hands. You know, whatever it took.
Well that was a little solo thing I did.
But I noticed, when you’re playing behind Dan, that you added some muscle, and when it got to the piano solo, that you went way down.

Well piano players — McKenna and Ralph — I mean that’s two Charles Atlases in a row right there. That’s strong players. Ross Tompkins got it all down, you know. That’s strength. Ralph doesn’t need anybody and neither does Dave. They’re an entity. They’re phenomenal those guys.
So instead of trying to battle with their strength, you let them take it.
